deep.reconstruction:
Context (from the neighbouring pages): Grothendieck is studying systems of pseudo-lines in the real projective plane X (most likely X = P^2(R)) and how such systems specialize. For a pseudo-line D, cutting X along D gives a closed disc Δ_D. Its boundary circle maps 2:1 onto D, and the antipodal map of ∂Δ_D is the deck involution. On ∂Δ_D there are privileged arcs: b, the transition arc, and b', its antipodal arc. On ∂Δ_{D'} there are the two transition arcs a and a'. For a specialization D → D', he glues Δ_D to Δ_{D'} along one arc α ∈ {a, a'} and one arc β ∈ {b, b'}. This gives 'eight standard ways' to build a surface with boundary whose associated graph is Γ. Up to composing with the antipodisms one may take β = b.

On this page he asks which choice of α gives a natural map from the glued surface 𝔛 into X, with Δ_D → X and Δ_{D'} → X the canonical maps.

(1) Naive requirement. The gluing arcs b and α must have the same image segment in X. That forces α = a.

(2) Shrinking trick. Replace Δ_D by a smaller disc Δ_D^* whose boundary passes through the vertex s (dotted line in the small pencil figure), and move b to b^*. Do the same for Δ_{D'}, so that the images of a and a' coincide in X. Then a map of the glued surface into X exists even for the other choice. (The transcription repeats 'α = a' here; by the logic it should be the other arc, and the next page confirms the adjustment b^* ∩ a^* ⊂ X is needed for α = a. So the page's labelling of a/a' is somewhat fluid.)

(3) Preferred choice. Nevertheless the most natural choice, whenever one wants a map to X, seems to be α = a'. With it the glued domain continues one bank (rive) of the critical strip by the other, and 𝔛 → X is an immersion. The coloured figure shows this:
- two red pseudo-lines crossing at a point;
- a green pseudo-line ω_D above and a yellow-green line ω_D' below, moving through the crossing (a triangle flip / triple-point passage);
- hatched strips ω and ω' on either side of the dotted critical segment where the gluing happens.

The arc of ∂Δ_{D'} that captures the generalization of D' towards D is the one that 'faces' (a'). It is not the arc obtained by 'parallel transport' along the specialization deformation D → D'. Grothendieck finds this choice 'parfaitement naturel'. The next page uses it to detect an orientation error committed earlier in the notes.

Purpose: to build a combinatorial/topological model (a surface glued from discs Δ_D, with an immersion into P^2) attached to a specialization of pseudo-line configurations. This is part of his attempt to understand the cell structure of the space of pseudo-line systems and the local moves (triangle flips) between them.
errors: The page uses 'α = a' in two places where the argument requires opposite choices: first α = a is forced, then 'even choosing α = a' after shrinking. One occurrence is probably a slip for α = a' (or the transcription misreads a prime). Grothendieck himself, on the next page, says he must re-examine whether he 'mixed things up' and finds an earlier orientation error.
The argument is heuristic: no proof that 𝔛 → X is an immersion for α = a' beyond the local picture; the shrinking construction Δ_D^* is only sketched.

ideas.what: Cutting RP^2 along a pseudo-line D gives a disc Δ_D whose boundary double-covers D with the antipodal involution; privileged transition and antipodal arcs on the boundary.
ideas.modern_name: Affine chart / cutting the projective plane along a line (the Möbius band complement)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (standard topology of RP^2; used in pseudoline theory by Levi 1926, Ringel, Grünbaum)

ideas.what: Gluing the discs of D and D' along transition arcs to model a specialization D → D', and choosing the arc so that the glued surface maps to X by an immersion.
ideas.modern_name: Local model of a mutation (triangle flip / Reidemeister-III-type move) in a pseudoline arrangement; gluing charts along a wall
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mutations of pseudoline arrangements: Ringel (1956); wiring diagrams and allowable sequences: Goodman–Pollack (1980s)

ideas.what: Distinguishing the 'facing' bank (a') from the bank obtained by 'parallel transport' during the deformation, and preferring the former as canonical.
ideas.modern_name: Monodromy / transport across a wall in a stratified configuration space

missed.claim: Grothendieck tries to attach to each specialization of pseudo-line systems a glued surface with a canonical immersion into P^2, depending on a choice of transition arc. He settles provisionally on the 'facing' arc a' but leaves the general construction and its relation to the 'holes' and vertices unresolved (next page).
missed.quote: Le choix le plus naturel quand même ... semblerait α = a' ... l'application 𝔛 → X est une immersion.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Only as part of the largely unstudied 1983–84 pseudo-line manuscript. The local content resembles well-known mutation/flip models in oriented matroid theory, so the novelty is minor.

deep.surprise_reason: A technical, self-correcting working page on gluing conventions for the local model of a pseudoline specialization. The geometry is elementary and close to standard flip/mutation pictures. There is no finished uncredited result here; it is of interest only as documentation of Grothendieck's process.
transcription_corrections: 'ce qui imposer α = a' → 'ce qui imposerait α = a'.
'une application de C surface recollée' → 'une application de la surface recollée'.
'(chaque fois dans une application dans X)' is likely '(chaque fois qu'on veut une application dans X)'.
'qui capture l' [-spécialisation-] {+généralisation+} spécialisation de vers D' → 'qui capture la généralisation de D' vers D'.
'la rive a, et non a qui en est déduite' should read 'la rive a', et non a qui en est déduite' (prime missing on the first a).
'Donc, mais le terrain est donné en continuation d'une rive par le deuxième' is uncertain; the sense is roughly that the glued domain is the continuation of one bank by the other.
'les rideaux (semble-t-il)' is doubtful; probably refers to the identifications/maps Δ_D → X, Δ_{D'} → X being canonical.
The first line beginning '[-pourtant-] au cas ... deux applications canoniques distinctes' likely reads 'pour lesquels il y a deux applications canoniques distinctes ... dans X!'.
